3fd730e04a05:
Specialists say that this icon painted on glass (thought to come from the mid-19th century, in northern Transylvania) is a combination of Orthodox and Catholic elements.

Icon painters of every age have tried to show the Mother of God as beautiful, gentle, dignified and glorified as possible. Sometimes they painted her saddened, sometimes sorrowful, but always full of spiritual strength and wisdom. The All-pure one is always shown with her head covered by a veil falling onto her shoulders, according to the Jewish tradition of those times. In most icons, the Mother of God holds the Child on her left arm and points to Him with her right hand; this icon, painted on anti-reflective glass, is one of the versions in which the Child is held in her right hand.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
a16abe56b904:
The theme of this icon is Saints Constantine and Helen, the Emperors.

Gaius Flavius Valerius Aurelius Constantinus (born 272/274 – died May 337), also known as Constantine I or Constantine the Great, was Roman emperor from 306 to 337, becoming ruler of the whole Roman Empire after defeating Maxentius and Licinius. Flavia Julia Helena (248–329), the wife of the Roman general Constantius Chlorus, was the mother of the holy Emperor Constantine the Great. She was a woman of great faith, known for her piety. She made a pilgrimage to Palestine and the eastern provinces, and tradition credits her with finding the Holy Cross of Christ and the remains of the three Magi.

The feast of Saints Constantine and Helen is one of the most important for Christians, because Emperor Constantine freed them from pagan persecution (by the Edict of Milan, in 313), and all his work, guided by the counsel of his mother Helen, was devoted to protecting the new religion.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
bb714ccf5075:
Typical of the Nicula area is the icon of “the Table of Paradise”, showing a rhombus-shaped table with the Virgin Mary, the Saviour Jesus Christ and two saints. In this icon (after a model from the first half of the 19th century), the two saints are Saint Nicholas and Saint Paraskeva.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
e41a6496842d:
The theme of this icon is the Annunciation, celebrated by the Orthodox Church every year on 25 March: the day on which the Holy Archangel Gabriel brings to Earth the news of the Birth of the Son of God. He comes to a town in Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, and announces to her that she will give birth to the Messiah. The virgin's name was Mary – the Holy Virgin Mary. The good news given to mankind about the incarnation of the Son of God in fact completes our personal feast, our own annunciation.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
f7f8ad84e9c3:
Every year on 6 December, the faithful celebrate one of the most beloved saints, Saint Nicholas. He is also called “the wonderworker” for the many miracles he worked even during his lifetime. There are many legends about Saint Nicholas, and several customs and traditions are linked to his day. The best known is the giving of gifts: on the eve of the feast, 5 December, children (and adults too – why not?) put their boots by the window or the door, and Saint Nicholas fills them with gifts. To the naughtiest, though, he brings a little switch.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
3e0f0a644bce:
On 20 July the Romanian Orthodox Church celebrates the ascent into heaven of the Holy Great Prophet Elijah the Tishbite (he came from Tishbe). One of the most important prophets of the Old Testament, Saint Elijah is honoured as a great wonderworker and bringer of rain in times of drought.

Depicted in icons either at the mouth of his cave, fed by a raven, or in the chariot of fire in which he was taken up to heaven, the Holy Great Prophet Elijah is, in the Church calendar and in folk tradition, the Old Testament figure most familiar to the Christian conscience, and the New Testament suggests that he will be the Forerunner of the second coming of Jesus.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
aac269c6eae3:
The theme of this icon is the Feast of the Holy Archangels Michael (“the power of God”) and Gabriel (“man of God”), set in the Byzantine calendar on 8 November and in the Latin calendar on 29 September. These saints are the patrons of many churches, known as the leaders of the choirs of angels, the guardians of people from birth to death and the guides of souls on their way to Paradise.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
eac8f535871b:
The theme of this icon (Nicula, late 18th century) is the Nativity of the Lord.

On 25 December Christians all over the world celebrate Christmas, the Feast of the Nativity of the Lord. More than two thousand years ago, the Virgin Mary (by the power of the Holy Spirit) gave birth to the Child Jesus in Bethlehem of Judea, in a poor manger. Then the three Magi from the East saw a bright star in the sky and, travelling a long way to follow it, reached Bethlehem, bringing the Saviour gifts of gold, myrrh and frankincense. Christmas as we know it today dates from the year 325; until then, pre-Christian religions marked the winter solstice at the same time of year.

Hand-painted on glass in tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The stained fir frame is also handmade.
